the association between socioeconomic status and life satisfaction was significantly moderated by perceived social capital in a community, and that this effect was stronger for pupils from low socioeconomic families.
the relationship between socioeconomic position and adolescents' life satisfaction is weaker in communities that have a higher degree of community social capital.
the social gradient was flattened when pupils had higher levels of perceived community cognitive social capital.

how social capital moderates the association between socioeconomic status and life satisfaction.
the role of social capital in the context of socioeconomic inequalities in adolescent life satisfaction.
the relationship between socioeconomic position (SEP), community social capital and adolescent life satisfaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

community social capital moderating the association between socioeconomic status and life satisfaction, while the cognitive component of community social capital is directly associated with life satisfaction.
community social capital has a moderating effect on the relationship between SES and adolescent life satisfaction.
the relationship between socioeconomic position and life satisfaction is moderated by the perception of social capital.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
community social capital is a resource which can be utilized by adolescents to enhance their life satisfaction and well being, and this resource is not equally distributed across the population.
the relationship between socioeconomic position and life satisfaction among adolescents is mediated by social capital and moderated by perceived community social capital.
social capital is an important factor that should be considered when developing policies aimed at improving adolescents' life satisfaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social capital is a complex construct, with both direct and indirect associations with adolescent life satisfaction.
community social capital is not only important in its own right for the well being of adolescents, but also in its potential to mitigate the negative effects of socioeconomic inequalities.
the relationship between SES and life outcomes is not necessarily fixed, but may be influenced by community social capital.
